provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 7 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: adesto -> desto; supplicationibus -> supplica xx tionibus; concede -> con cede; animabus -> animdbus; curandis -> curdndis; deuoto -> deu to; celebremus -> celebre mus per d minum; 1922 Mame text layer damages 2 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): adesto -> pesto; supplicationibus -> suppli a cationibus; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 79, artifact PDF p. 193; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 26676 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.text:
Adesto, Domine, supplicationibus nostris: et concede; ut hoc solemne
jejunium, quod animabus corporibusque curandis salubriter institutum est,
devoto servitio celebremus. Per Dominum nostrum.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1962 prints the conclusion written out (14 words); the public-domain witnesses abbreviate it to the short cue; 1862 text layer damages 6 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: suscipe domine -> d mine; uoluisti dignanter -> uolufsti digndnter; placari presta quesumus -> plac ri pnesta qu tsumusi; operatione mundati beneplacitum -> operatio ne munddti beneplacituni; nostre -> nostne; offeramus affectum -> offerdmus affe ctum per d minum ali; 1922 Mame text layer damages 4 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): suscipe -> (absent from the aligned window); immolatione -> immolati ne; quesumus -> queesumus; operatione -> operatiene; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 80, artifact PDF p. 194; the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Sabbato post cineres) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Secreta the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Suscipe, Domine, sacrificium, cujus te voluisti dignanter immolatione
placari: praesta, quaesumus; ut, hujus operatione mundati, beneplacitum tibi
nostrae mentis offeramus affectum. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum,
Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.
